# Didgeridoo Healing Center
cbDIDG Method - Eyal Amit

## Didgeridoo-based breath work, sound healing, learning and training in Pardes Hanna, Israel

For more than 25 years, the didgeridoo has been at the center of my work with breath, sound and people.

I use the instrument not only as something to play, but as a practical tool for developing breath awareness, coordination, presence and a deeper relationship with the body.

Over the years, this work developed into **cbDIDG**, a structured method that brings together didgeridoo playing, breathing practice, sound and body awareness.

Today, the Didgeridoo Healing Center in Pardes Hanna offers one-on-one breath work, didgeridoo lessons, private sound healing, workshops, talks, advanced learning and handmade instruments.

**English-speaking visitors are welcome.**

[**Talk to Eyal on WhatsApp**](https://wa.me/972524822842?text=Hi%20Eyal%2C%20I%20found%20you%20through%20the%20English%20page)

---

## More than learning an instrument

### Working with breath through the didgeridoo

The didgeridoo is usually introduced as an ancient wind instrument.

In my work, I see it first and foremost as a **breath-training instrument**.

Playing requires coordination between breathing, lips, tongue, cheeks, throat and attention. The instrument provides immediate feedback. When the breath changes, the sound changes.

This makes the didgeridoo an unusually direct tool for exploring the way we breathe.

My approach is active.

You are not simply receiving a treatment while someone else plays. You learn, practice, listen, adjust and gradually develop skills you can continue using independently.

The goal is not musical performance.

**The instrument is the practice tool. The breath is the work.**

---

# The cbDIDG Method

## A structured method developed through more than two decades of practice

Over the years I developed **cbDIDG**, my method for working with breathing through the didgeridoo.

The method grew gradually from several worlds that became connected through my own experience:

* more than 25 years of playing and teaching didgeridoo
* my apprenticeship with Mukesh Dahiman in India
* years of building didgeridoos by hand
* study and practice of tai chi, qigong, yoga and mindfulness
* my background as an electronics engineer
* my interest in physiology, acoustics and the mechanics of breathing
* thousands of hours of individual work with students and clients

Three principles are central to the method.

### Active work

The person participates in the process.

The work is learned through practice rather than received passively.

### The didgeridoo is the tool, not the goal

Learning to produce sound, coordinate the breathing system and eventually develop circular breathing creates a practical framework for exploring breath patterns, control, awareness and attention.

You do not need to become a musician.

### Change develops through repetition

This work is not built around a one-time experience.

Skills develop through guided practice, repetition and gradual independent work.

---

# Why breath became my life's work

My relationship with breathing began long before I understood that it would eventually become my profession.

When I was twelve, the apartment building where I lived in Givatayim caught fire. A friend from the building died in that fire, and the experience stayed with me.

Years later, during my military service, I developed severe asthma and allergies.

For a long time I lived with wheezing, medication, inhalers and the feeling that breathing itself had become difficult.

Then I encountered the didgeridoo.

At first, I was simply drawn to its sound.

I wanted to understand how this strange instrument could produce a continuous, deep tone, so I began learning to play.

Only gradually did I begin to notice what the practice was asking me to do.

Slow down.

Coordinate.

Listen.

Pay attention.

Develop control without force.

And, most importantly, build a completely different relationship with my own breath.

My personal experience with asthma and breathing was one of the forces that led me to study the subject more deeply.

I do not present my experience as a medical promise for someone else.

But it shaped the question that has guided my work ever since:

**What can happen when a person learns to work consciously, patiently and consistently with their own breathing?**

That question eventually became the foundation of my professional work.

---

# My teacher, Mukesh Dahiman

## Craftsmanship, patience and a way of working

I first met **Mukesh Dahiman** in Rishikesh, India, in 2000.

Mukesh was a didgeridoo maker, teacher and craftsman who came from a family tradition of woodworking. Over many years he devoted himself to building didgeridoos and teaching people who arrived in Rishikesh from around the world.

I returned to study with him and became one of his close students.

What I learned from Mukesh went far beyond the technical skills of making or playing an instrument.

His workshop taught me patience, craftsmanship, repetition, listening and respect for a process that cannot be rushed.

These principles remain deeply connected to the way I work today.

Mukesh passed away in October 2020.

His influence continues through the instruments I build, the way I teach and the knowledge I pass on to others.

---

# Ways to work with me

## One-on-one didgeridoo breath work

Individual sessions are at the core of my work.

We begin by looking at the way you breathe and understanding what brings you to the studio.

From there, I develop a personal practice process according to the individual.

A session may include:

* initial observation and assessment
* a personalized practice plan
* practical breathing exercises
* didgeridoo-based exercises
* coordination of lips, cheeks, tongue, diaphragm and airflow
* sound and body awareness
* development of independent practice skills
* listening, attention and presence

The objective is gradually to give you more understanding and greater awareness of your own breathing.

No previous musical experience is required.

Sessions take place one-on-one at my studio in Pardes Hanna, Israel.

---

# Didgeridoo Lessons

## Learn to play from the beginning

You can also come simply because you want to learn this extraordinary instrument.

Private didgeridoo lessons are available from complete beginner level onward.

Learning can include:

* producing the basic drone
* understanding airflow and breath control
* circular breathing
* rhythm
* tongue techniques
* vocal techniques
* overtones
* sound development
* musical expression
* developing a personal practice

My approach to teaching is detailed and gradual.

Complex movements are broken down into simple components, practiced separately and then connected.

For many students, learning the didgeridoo becomes much more than learning another musical instrument.

The process naturally develops attention to breathing, concentration and body awareness.

---

# Private Sound Healing

## A different way to experience the didgeridoo

Sound healing is a very different experience from active breath work.

During a private didgeridoo sound session, you do not need to learn, play or practice.

You lie down and receive the sound.

The low drone, harmonics, rhythms and physical vibration of the didgeridoo create an immersive listening experience that many people experience as relaxing, grounding and meditative.

Sessions are available for individuals and couples.

### Breath work or sound healing?

The distinction is important.

**Didgeridoo breath work is active.**
You learn, practice and gradually build skills.

**Sound healing is receptive.**
You listen and experience the sound.

Both involve the didgeridoo, but they are two very different forms of work.

---

# Workshops

## Breath, sound and didgeridoo as a shared experience

I lead experiential didgeridoo workshops for groups, organizations, private events and communities.

Participants do not need any previous musical experience.

The workshops combine explanation, live demonstration and active participation.

They offer a direct introduction to the relationship between breathing, sound, attention and the didgeridoo.

Workshops usually last approximately **90 to 120 minutes** and can be adapted to the group and setting.

They are suitable for:

* private groups
* organizations
* company teams
* retreats
* wellness programs
* community groups
* special events

The emphasis is on participation and direct experience.

---

# Talks

## Breath, health, sound and the story behind the instrument

My talks combine personal story, professional experience, research and live didgeridoo demonstrations.

Depending on the audience, talks can explore themes connected to:

* breathing and health
* stress
* sleep
* sound and vibration
* the nervous system
* the didgeridoo
* my personal journey with breathing
* the path from electronics engineering to didgeridoo-based breath work

Unlike workshops, talks are primarily designed for a listening audience.

They are available for companies, organizations, conferences, professional events, communities and private groups.

---

# Learning and Professional Training

## Taking the work further

Alongside individual work and group activities, the educational side of cbDIDG continues to grow.

I offer and develop advanced learning opportunities for people who want to explore the field more deeply.

These may include:

* advanced didgeridoo study
* courses
* professional education
* therapeutic applications of didgeridoo practice
* future practitioner training connected to the cbDIDG method

Some programs are intended for experienced players or professionals, while others are suitable for people who simply want to deepen their understanding.

For current courses and training opportunities, contact me directly.

---

# What does research say about the didgeridoo?

Scientific research into didgeridoo-related practices is still limited.

It is therefore important to distinguish between promising findings and established medical evidence.

Several studies are particularly interesting.

## Snoring and obstructive sleep apnea

A randomized controlled trial published in the *British Medical Journal* examined adults with snoring and moderate obstructive sleep apnea.

Participants in the didgeridoo group received lessons and practiced regularly for four months.

Compared with the control group, the didgeridoo group showed improvements in:

* daytime sleepiness
* apnea-hypopnea index
* their partners' reported sleep disturbance

The study included only 25 participants, so the findings are promising but should not be interpreted as definitive evidence.

## Stress and relaxation

A randomized study involving 74 university students compared a 30-minute live didgeridoo sound meditation with silent breath meditation.

Both groups reported increased relaxation.

Participants in the didgeridoo meditation group experienced significantly greater relaxation and lower acute self-perceived stress than participants in the silent meditation group.

## Mood, stress and autonomic regulation

Another study followed 20 beginners through ten didgeridoo-based health promotion lessons.

Researchers reported changes in measures related to:

* mood
* mental stress
* pulse
* salivary amylase
* autonomic nervous system balance

These studies are part of a relatively small body of research.

They do not establish didgeridoo practice as a replacement for medical treatment, but they do support continued investigation into the instrument as a tool connected to breathing, sound and wellbeing.

---

# Handmade Didgeridoos

## From wood to sound

Building didgeridoos has been part of my life almost as long as playing them.

I learned instrument making in India with Mukesh Dahiman and later continued developing my craft in Israel.

My background in electronics engineering also influenced the way I think about instruments.

A didgeridoo is acoustically much more complex than it may appear.

Its:

* length
* internal bore
* geometry
* diameter
* resistance
* material
* shape

all influence the way the instrument responds and the sound it produces.

I build didgeridoos by hand, including instruments made from agave.

The studio also offers:

* handmade didgeridoos
* professional instruments
* instrument repair
* restoration
* carrying bags
* stands and accessories
* guidance in choosing the right instrument

If you are looking for a didgeridoo, you are welcome to contact me and arrange a visit to the workshop.

---

# About Eyal Amit

I have been working with the didgeridoo since **1999**.

Over the years I have worked as a player, teacher, instrument maker and practitioner using the didgeridoo as a tool for working with breathing.

My original professional training was in electronics engineering.

My path later moved through woodworking, writing, publishing, performance and storytelling, but the didgeridoo gradually became the center of my professional life.

Today I am the founder of the **Didgeridoo Healing Center** in Pardes Hanna and the developer of the **cbDIDG method**.

From my studio I work with people individually, teach didgeridoo, build instruments and lead workshops, talks and sound healing sessions.

What connects all of these activities is one simple idea:

**Breathing is something we do every moment of our lives, but it is also something we can learn to observe, practice and understand more deeply.**

The didgeridoo gives us an unusual and powerful way to do that.

## Pardes Hanna, Israel

The center is located in Pardes Hanna, surrounded by a garden and designed as a quiet space for individual and group work.

It includes both the studio where I teach and work with people and the workshop where I build and repair didgeridoos.

People come from different parts of Israel and from abroad for:

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Do I need to know how to play the didgeridoo?

No.

Most people begin with no previous experience.

The process starts with basic breathing, sound production and simple coordination.

---

## Do I need to own a didgeridoo before I start?

No.

You can begin with instruments available at the studio.

If you later decide to buy an instrument, I can help you understand what type of didgeridoo is suitable for you.

---

## Do I need musical experience?

No.

Musical experience can be useful, but it is not necessary for breath work, beginner didgeridoo lessons or workshops.

---

## Is this medical treatment?

The work offered at the center is complementary and educational and is not a substitute for medical diagnosis or treatment.

If you have a medical condition, including a respiratory or sleep-related condition, you should continue to consult your physician or other qualified healthcare professional.

---

## Can didgeridoo practice replace CPAP or other medical treatment for sleep apnea?

No medical treatment should be stopped or changed without consultation with the healthcare professional responsible for your care.

Research into didgeridoo playing and obstructive sleep apnea is interesting, but it remains limited.

---

## Is didgeridoo breath work the same as sound healing?

No.

Didgeridoo breath work is an active learning process.

Sound healing is primarily a receptive listening experience.

---

## Can complete beginners join a workshop?

Yes.

The workshops are designed so that participants with no background in music or didgeridoo can take part.

---

## Do you work in English?

Yes.

Private sessions, didgeridoo lessons and selected workshops can be conducted in English.

---

## Where is the center?

The Didgeridoo Healing Center is located in **Pardes Hanna, Israel**.

**תאריכים חדשים יפורסמו בקרוב**

אם רציתם לפגוש את כלי הריפוי הקדום הזה מקרוב, להתנסות בו בעצמכם, ללמוד על איכויותיו התרפויטיות, להדק את הקשר עם הנשימה שלכם וליהנות מחווית סאונד הילינג עוצמתית, הסדנה הייחודית הזו נתפרה במיוחד בשבילכם!

כמה דברים שחשוב לקרוא ולדעת לפני:
•	הסדנה מיועדת לגילאי 18 ומעלה ולאלה שלא מנגנים עדיין בדיג'רידו. זו סדנה למתחילים בלבד ואיננה מתאימה למי שכבר נושם מעגלית בדיג'רידו.
 
•	הסדנה הינה התנסות ראשונית, טעימה, ואינה מבטיחה שבעקבותיה תוכלו לנשום מעגלית בדיג'רידו, על מנת להגיע לשלב הזה בדרך כלל נדרש תרגול רב וסדרה של מפגשים.
 
•	הסדנה אינה מתאימה לחולי לב, נשים בהריון או לסובלים מלחץ דם. 
 
•	מספר המשתתפים בכל סדנה מוגבל. השאיפה לשמור על קבוצה אינטימית ונעימה.
 
•	חניה יש בשפע במרחק דקה הליכה מהסטודיו (בסמוך לבריכת הלוויתן, פינת רחוב קק"ל-מעפילים).
 
•	הסדנה תתקיים בכל מזג אוויר.
 
•	במידה ואין ברשותכם דיג'רידו, במסגרת הסדנה ינתן לכל משתתף צינור תרגול אישי מפלסטיק עם פיה נוחה לשפתיים. בתום הסדנה תעמוד בפניכם האפשרות לרכוש את צינור התרגול.
 
•	לא תתאפשר כניסה עם כלבים. את ידידנו הנפלאים ההולכים על ארבע בבקשה תשאירו בבית.

דידג'רידו הוא כלי נשיפה קדום בעל תו אחד שפותח על ידי תושביה המקוריים של אוסטרליה, האבוריג'ינים. בשני העשורים האחרונים בוצעו מחקרים מדעיים רבים אודות השפעותיו התרפויטיות והוכחה יעילותו ככלי טיפולי בהתמודדות עם מצבי הסטרס הכרוני והסימפטומים הנלווים אליו.
אייל עמית, מורה לנשימה נכונה ומלווה תהליכי ריפוי באמצעות נשימה בדיג'רידו בשיטה ייחודית שפיתח, המביא עמו ניסיון של 26 שנים (מאז 1999) בתחום הדיג'רידו, הוא מוותיקי הנגנים, הבנאים, המורים והמטפלים בדידג'רידו בישראל ותלמידו הקרוב של המאסטר ההודי מוקש דהימן בשני העשורים האחרונים. את המרכז לטיפול בדיג'רידו – המרכז לטיפול בנשימה באמצעות דיג'רידו פרדס חנה הקים במטרה לקדם, להפיץ וללמד את איכויותיו התרפויטיות של הדיג'רידו בתחומי הגוף, הנפש והתודעה.
